prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1456; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Loss reported by the insured driver, who states the vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The other driver has been identified and is named on the policy.
Entry 2: Recorded the insured's account by phone. The insured describes a slow turn across the oncoming lane and a light contact to the front quarter panel of the vehicle.
Entry 3: Police report obtained. The responding officer confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and notes the collision was consistent with a left-turn impact.
Entry 4: Scene photographs and two independent witness statements received. Both witnesses describe the collision as the insured described it.
Entry 5: Inspected the insured vehicle. The visible damage lines up with the reported impact point, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or from the repair history.
Entry 6: Bodily injury claim opened after the claimant's attorney contacted us. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is now represented.
Entry 7: Reviewed the medical records. The reported injury seems severe for an impact this light, though the claimant has been consistent about symptoms and has not described the accident differently in any conversation.
Entry 8: Checked prior claims and medical history. No earlier injury to the neck or back has been identified for this claimant.
Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course of care, with frequency tapering as the claimant's reported improvement continued. No gaps or unusual procedures noted in the billing.
Entry 10: Coverage confirmed as active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.
Entry 11: Discussed the file with the claimant's attorney, who restated the accident account and asked for an evaluation of the injury claim. Response to be prepared after the treating physician's final report arrives.
Entry 12: Current status: liability facts are supported by the police report, witnesses, photos and the other driver's account. The injury evaluation remains open pending final medical review and attorney correspondence.
